newsitem.title: JAPAN: Scandal won't undermine Nomura, DKB health - BOJ.
newsitem.headline: Scandal won't undermine Nomura, DKB health - BOJ.

text.p: Bank of Japan Governor Yasuo Matsushita said on Wednesday that the central bank does not see the scandal involving Nomura Securities Co Ltd and Dai-Ichi Kangyo Bank Ltd (DKB) undermining their financial soundness.
Matsushita said in a statement: "The Bank of Japan does not see the scandal over Dai-Ichi Kangyo Bank and Nomura Securities greatly undermining their financial soundness."

"However, the central bank strongly hopes that they put in place internal control systems that would avoid a recurrence of the scandal, which in turn could help recover confidence (in the industry) both at home and abroad," Matsushita said.
The Bank of Japan has demanded DKB and Nomura take measures to improve internal administration to avoid recurrence of the scandals, Matsushita said.
The central bank will be briefed on the progress of concrete steps from both institutions and will make sure they actually get implemented, he said.

"The central bank will, in view of these scandals, urge other financial institutions to further strengthen their risk control systems, including internal control, through regular inspections," Matsushita said.
